section_1.title: Defining the Vector: Movement in Space
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of a vector as an ordered pair representing magnitude and direction, distinct from a single point. Visualize this as an arrow starting at the origin (0,0) and ending at a specific coordinate.
section_1.example: A 'Robot Dog' starting at the charging station (0,0) moves to position (3, 2). The vector v = [3, 2] describes this displacement.

section_2.title: Scalar Multiplication: Stretching the Path
section_2.content: Explain how multiplying a vector by a scalar (a real number) changes its length but keeps its direction (or reverses it). Use a scaling animation to show the vector growing or shrinking along the same line.
section_2.example: The 'Robot Dog' runs twice as fast, effectively doubling its displacement vector: 2 * [3, 2] = [6, 4].

section_3.title: Vector Addition: Combining Forces
section_3.content: Introduce vector addition using the 'Tip-to-Tail' method. Visually demonstrate placing the start of the second vector at the tip of the first to find the final resultant position.
section_3.example: The 'Robot Dog' first moves [3, 2] to find a ball, then moves [1, -3] to find a bone. The total displacement is [3+1, 2-3] = [4, -1].

section_4.title: Linear Combinations: The Basis of Space
section_4.content: Explain how any point in a 2D plane can be reached by combining the basis vectors (i = [1,0] and j = [0,1]). This serves as the foundation for defining span and coordinate systems.
section_4.example: Think of the 'Robot Dog' moving on a grid. To reach any point (x, y), it simply moves 'x' units along the x-axis and 'y' units along the y-axis, representing the combination: x[1,0] + y[0,1].

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text("- " + line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
